name: Tea
lede: Tea is a light green that Maerz and Paul date to 1829, and among the rarest colors in our painting archive, matching only seven paintings out of nearly 24,000.

sections.title: A plant word, not the drink's own color
sections.body: Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary dates Tea to 1829 and places it on plate 19, swatch A4; the 1955 ISCC-NBS system classes it as a grayish yellow green, block 122 [1]. The xkcd survey and Wikipedia both independently land on a near-identical swatch, within about 1.4 units of CIEDE2000 [1]. The name describes the plant's leaf, not the brewed drink, or [[tan]] [1]. The nearest named color on file is [[verdigris-green]], 2.8 ΔE off [1]. A separate, paler library entry, [[tea-green]], names the same plant [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds a close match to Tea in only 7 of 23,781 paintings, about one in 3,400, as photographed, too rare for any reliable painter or color pairing [2]. It splits about evenly between highlight and midtone roles in those few appearances [2]. The earliest dated match is a painting cataloged as *Horizon of the New World*, from 1830, one year after Maerz and Paul's own date, an unusually close agreement for this library, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2].

origin.first_recorded: Maerz and Paul, 1930 (first recorded 1829, plate 19 A4)

questions.q: What does the name Tea describe: the plant's leaf, or the brewed drink?
choices: Neither — it is a dye name

questions.q: True or false: Tea is one of the more common colors in our painting archive.

openers: Tea names the plant's green leaf, not the brown of the drink it's brewed into.
